claim: For every connected complete multipartite graph \(G=K_{n_1,\ldots,n_r}\) with \(r\ge2\), the outer mutual-visibility chromatic number is \(1\) exactly when \(G\) is complete and is \(2\) otherwise. The dual mutual-visibility chromatic number is \(1\) when \(G\) is complete, is infinite exactly for stars \(K_{1,n}\) with \(n\ge3\), and is \(2\) in every other case. The total mutual-visibility chromatic number is \(1\) when \(G\) is complete, is infinite exactly for stars \(K_{1,n}\) with \(n\ge2\), and is \(2\) in every other case.
integrity: The total-star obstruction and the general outer one-color lower bound are explicitly treated as prior coverage. The accepted claim is the complete-multipartite classification, with the dual boundary and uniform two-color constructions proved directly.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to finite connected complete multipartite graphs. The finite verifier checks only profiles of order at most eight and is not used as an infinite proof. Very recent or unindexed equivalent literature may remain.
title: Dual, outer, and total mutual-visibility colorings of complete multipartite graphs
